summary: Ephemeral sidechain burst causing regional GPU squeeze and autoscaler undershoot
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC we observed a sustained p99 latency spike and reduced reserved GPU attach rates in CobaltAI's dedicated pool in us-west-2. Impact: Customer reports 40-60% reduction in throughput for batched routes and 5xx spikes for streaming requests. Autoscaler did not provision additional GPUs during the event, and several tenants experienced throttling.

Environment: Dedicated pool (cust-reserved-44), production, us-west-2, customer tier=dedicated.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer runs multi-tenant inference with mixed short/long-streams using SDK v2. 2) Background analytics sidecar scheduled a high-frequency sample upload sweep. 3) Within minutes, batch queue lengths grew and attach latency to GPUs increased. 4) Autoscaler cooldown prevented new allocations for ~6 minutes.

Observed behavior: Sudden burst of small sidecar uploads coincided with a large number of short-lived connections from customer workers. This created ephemeral connection fanout, noisy-prefetch IO on NVMe, and elevated CUDA attach times. Autoscaler heuristics misclassified the signal as transient and did not scale, causing regional GPU thinness and cross-tenant contention.

Expected behavior: Autoscaler should detect sustained queue growth and schedule capacity or fallback earlier; sidecar I/O should be rate-limited to avoid platform-wide attach penalties.

Relevant logs/metrics: See linked graphs for attach_latency, allocator_pending, gpu_attach_failures, nvme_io_wait. Affected routes show increased serialization and batch fragmentation.

Customer impact & timeframe: Intermittent throughput collapse for ~25 minutes during the morning window; customer batch jobs saw tail-loss and multiple retries.

Temporary workaround: Apply sidecar client throttling and enable short-lived-conn coalescing on client side. Support suggested immediate rate-limit rule on customer's analytics sidecar to reduce connection rate by 80%.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel (Support): Notified SRE after initial triage; provided customer request IDs and sample SDK traces. Asked for early signal if this maps to known allocator regressions.

2026-03-10 | Mateo Alvarez (SRE): Observed NVMe IO wait spike (hosted telemetry). Prefetcher and analytics sidecar generated a 3k/s file upload burst from the customer's infra. Autoscaler window is set to 60s smoothing; detected a short spike and suppressed scale-up due to hysteresis. Captured allocator timeline in /confluence/runbooks/dedicated-allocator-debug.

2026-03-10 | Jonas Reed (Eng): Reproduced attach latency with a local loadgen simulating small-stream fanout + NVMe stress. Hypothesis: sidecar upload threads saturate host IO and induce GPU driver attach latency; autoscaler rules need an additional 'attach_latency' metric to trigger earlier scale-up.

2026-03-11 | CobaltAI (Customer): Confirmed they rolled a temporary throttling policy and saw immediate improvement in throughput. Asked for permanent mitigation and guidance to avoid future regressions.

2026-03-12 | Jonas Reed (Eng): Deployed temporary autoscaler rule change to lower cooldown from 60s to 30s for this reserved pool; monitoring for noise amplification. Planning a hotfix to add attach_latency to autoscaler feature gating.
investigation_notes: Correlation: Attach latency spike co-occurs with NVMe io_wait and increased small-file uploads from customer's sidecar process.
Autoscaler behavior: Smoothing+cooldown prevented scale-up despite growing pending queue; threshold tuned for medium-length jobs, not short-stream fanouts.

Root causes: (1) Noisy sidecar causing host IO pressure; (2) attach_latency not included in autoscaler decision signals; (3) batcher fragmentation due to short stream interleaving increased effective GPU occupancy per tenant.

Mitigation tested: Applying rate limits on sidecar reduces attach_latency within 90s and restores attach rate. Lowering autoscaler cooldown to 30s triggers scale-up within 60-90s in tests but risks reacting to true transient spikes.
Telemetry links: slack thread #support-cobaltai, grafana panels (attach_latency, allocator_pending, nvme_io_wait), and trace ids: trace-20260310-12ab.
Related: partial overlap with SUP-3141592 (cohort coldstart burst) and SUP-531020 (microbatch saturation) — added as linked issues for cross-reference.
resolution:
Mitigation performed: 1) Customer applied sidecar upload rate-limits (recommended at 80% reduction); 2) Temporary autoscaler cooldown change applied to the specific reserved pool; 3) We scheduled a targeted hotfix to incorporate attach_latency into autoscaler signals and added a guard to ignore pure-IO transients. Customer throughput restored to expected levels after rate-limiting.

Follow-ups: Implement autoscaler signal change (ENG-2079), add a platform-side I/O backpressure policy for high-frequency uploaders, and update the dedicated runbook with sidecar throttling guidance. Plan verification window for 72 hours post-deploy.
